subject: project:gdl
value: REPORT (a list, not a rewrite -- no law's text was altered by this lane). 258 of 324 law-bearing claim records (predicates law/codegen_law/workflow_law) state their conclusion in NECESSITY language -- MUST, NEVER, ALWAYS, CANNOT, IS THE ONLY, IMPOSSIBLE, UNREACHABLE, source-unreachable, INVARIANT, 'there is no' -- while carrying NO falsifier: no falsifier/falsified_by/counterexample field, and no prose saying what evidence would disprove them. That is 80% of the corpus asserting universals with nothing recorded that could retire them. Why this matters here specifically: this project's own history is a record of such universals falling. Records in the corpus REFUTE earlier records' necessity claims by measurement ('THAT IS FALSE', 'THE FRAME-DELTA FRAMING IS AN ARTIFACT', 'PREMISE REFUTED BY MACHINE PROOF'), and AGENTS.md already codifies that a law's PRESCRIPTION rots faster than its diagnosis (3 of 6 cures wrong on one measured roster). A necessity claim with no falsifier cannot be screened cheaply, cannot expire, and is therefore indistinguishable from a claim that is merely old. The highest-risk subset is the 'source-unreachable' / 'CANNOT' family, because those laws are exactly the ones cited to justify parking a function or promoting it to the postprocessor path -- an unfalsifiable 'source-unreachable' is a permanent veto asserted on prose authority. RECOMMENDATION (integrator decision, not executed by this lane): require attributes.falsifier on any NEW law using necessity language, and backfill it authoritatively only by the law's own author or a lane that re-measures it -- this lane deliberately did not invent falsifiers for other agents' laws.
